title: Fundevogel
paragraphs: Once there was a forester who went into the forest to hunt. As he entered it, he heard screaming, as if a little child were there. He followed the sound and at last came to a tall tree. At the top of it sat a little child. The mother had fallen asleep under the tree with the child in her arms, and a bird of prey had seen it, swooped down, snatched it away, and set it on the high tree.

The forester climbed the tree, lifted the child down, and thought to himself, “I’ll take him home and raise him alongside my Lina.” So he carried the baby home, and the two children grew up side by side. The one he had found in the tree was named Fundevogel, since a bird had carried him off. Fundevogel and Lina were so fond of each other that whenever they were apart, they were miserable.

The forester had an old cook. One evening she picked up two pails and started fetching water from the spring, and she didn’t make just one trip but many. Lina noticed and asked, “Tell me, old Sanna, why are you carrying so much water?” “I’ll tell you, if you swear never to repeat it to anyone.” Lina promised that she would never tell a soul, and the cook said, “Early tomorrow morning, as soon as the forester has gone hunting, I’m going to heat up the water. When it’s boiling in the kettle, I’ll throw Fundevogel in and boil him.”

Early the next morning the forester got up and went off hunting. While he was away, the children were still lying in bed. Lina said to Fundevogel, “If you promise never to leave me, I’ll never leave you either.” Fundevogel answered, “I won’t leave you, now or ever.” Then Lina said, “Then I’ll tell you. Last night old Sanna hauled bucket after bucket of water into the house, so I asked her why. She said she would tell me if I promised not to repeat it to anyone. Then she told me that early tomorrow morning, when Father is out hunting, she will fill the kettle, throw you in and boil you. But let’s get up quickly, get dressed and run away together.”

So the two children got up, dressed in a hurry and left. When the water in the kettle was bubbling, the cook went to the bedroom to fetch Fundevogel and throw him in. But when she walked in and reached the beds, both children had vanished. She was horrified and said to herself, “What am I going to tell the forester when he comes home and finds the children gone? They have to be chased right now and brought back.”

The cook sent three servants to chase the children and catch them. But the children were sitting at the edge of the forest, and when they saw the three servants running toward them from far off, Lina said to Fundevogel, “Never leave me, and I’ll never leave you.” Fundevogel said, “Not now, not ever.” Then Lina said, “You turn into a rose-bush, and I’ll be the rose on it.” When the three servants reached the forest, there was nothing there but a rose-bush with one rose on it, and no sign of the children. “There’s nothing for us here,” they said, and they went home and told the cook that they had seen nothing in the forest except a little rose-bush with a single rose. The old cook scolded them. “You idiots! You should have cut the rose-bush in half, snapped off the rose and brought it back with you. Go and do it, now.” So they had to go out and search a second time. But the children saw them coming from a long way off. Lina said, “Fundevogel, never leave me, and I’ll never leave you.” Fundevogel said, “Not now, not ever.” Lina said, “Then you turn into a church, and I’ll be the chandelier inside it.” When the three servants arrived, there was nothing but a church with a chandelier in it. They said to each other, “What can we do here? Let’s go home.” When they got back, the cook asked whether they had found the children, and they said no, they had found nothing but a church with a chandelier inside. The cook scolded them again. “You fools! Why didn’t you tear the church down and bring the chandelier home?” This time the old cook got to her feet herself and set off with the three servants after the children. Once more the children saw, far off, the three servants coming and the cook waddling along behind them. Lina said, “Fundevogel, never leave me, and I’ll never leave you.” Fundevogel said, “Not now, not ever.” Lina said, “Then be a fishpond, and I’ll be the duck swimming on it.” The cook came up to them, and when she saw the pond, she lay down beside it and started to drink it dry. But the duck swam over fast, grabbed her head in its beak and pulled her into the water, and the old witch drowned there. Then the children went home together, very happy, and if they haven’t died, they’re still alive today.
